rubricScores.criterion: Identified that the signing target sweeps a distribution/output folder
Recognized that multiple projects write to the same output folder
Connected the access-denied error to file ownership or read-only constraints
Explained why the failure is non-deterministic
Suggested separating project outputs or removing redundant copy configurations
Efficiency and rigor of investigation

scenarios.reasoning: Strong, evidence-grounded diagnosis: isolated the single failing file among 40, noted the sibling in the same directory signed fine (ruling out ACLs), attributed the failure to a cross-project race on a shared output directory, explained the non-determinism, and gave prioritized fixes plus a falsifiable test. Falls short of excellent because it did not identify the read-only/hard-linked CAS output mechanism and could not directly confirm a concurrent writer in the binlog, leaving part of the causal chain inferred.
scenarios.scenario: Analysis — Diagnose why code signing fails with access denied

rubricScores.criterion: Found MSB3073 error in DataSources signing step and identified the specific failing file(s)
Traced failing file to its origin — placed in shared folder by a different project
Discovered multiple projects set Distrib to same ConfigurationLinterService path
Identified CAS read-only hard links as reason files are unsignable
Explained non-determinism via target ordering across projects
Proposed removing Distrib/Robocopy from library projects so one project owns the output folder
Verified the fix by confirming separated outputs mean each project signs only its own files

scenarios.reasoning: Efficient, methodical investigation with good binlog tool usage and correct identification of the error, failing file, and shared-output-folder pattern. However the central mechanistic conclusion (read-only CAS hard links) was actively rejected in favor of a concurrent-lock race, the shared-Distrib claim across sibling projects was asserted rather than verified, and several proposed fix properties appear fabricated. Confident presentation exceeds the evidence in places, and no verification step was performed.
